intro.Ara Damansara: Ara Damansara is a Petaling Jaya township near Subang Airport, with LRT stations and links to the Federal Highway.
intro.Bandar Sri Damansara: Bandar Sri Damansara is a mature township in north-west Kuala Lumpur and Petaling Jaya, close to Desa ParkCity and Kepong.
intro.Bangsar: Bangsar is a mature, leafy neighbourhood popular with expats and families, with Bangsar Village, Bangsar Shopping Centre and quick access to Mid Valley and KL Sentral.
intro.Bangsar South: Bangsar South is a transit-oriented city next to Kerinchi LRT station, with offices, Nexus, The Sphere and a 6-acre park.
intro.Batu Kawan: Batu Kawan is Penang's mainland growth area at the Second Penang Bridge, with IKEA, Design Village outlet mall and an industrial park.
intro.Bayan Lepas: Bayan Lepas in southern Penang island hosts the airport and the Free Industrial Zone, a major employment hub.
intro.Bukit Bintang: Bukit Bintang is KL's shopping and entertainment district, home to Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, Lot 10 and the Bukit Bintang City Centre (BBCC) development, served by MRT and Monorail stations.
intro.Bukit Jalil: Bukit Jalil in southern Kuala Lumpur grew around the National Stadium and is now anchored by Pavilion Bukit Jalil and the 80-acre Bukit Jalil Recreational Park, with LRT stations and direct highway links.
intro.Damansara Damai: Damansara Damai is a residential area in north Petaling Jaya, close to Damansara Perdana and the LDP.
intro.Damansara Heights: Damansara Heights is one of Kuala Lumpur's most established upmarket neighbourhoods, next to Pavilion Damansara Heights and the Semantan MRT station.
intro.Damansara Perdana: Damansara Perdana is a township in north Petaling Jaya near Mutiara Damansara and the Damansara–Puchong Expressway (LDP).
intro.Gelugor: Gelugor is on Penang island's east coast near the Penang Bridge and Universiti Sains Malaysia, and home to The Light City waterfront development.
intro.George Town: George Town is Penang's UNESCO World Heritage capital, with the island's main shopping, food and business addresses.
intro.JB City Centre: Johor Bahru City Centre is next to the Causeway, the JB CIQ checkpoint and the upcoming RTS Link station at Bukit Chagar.
intro.Johor: Johor Bahru sits across the Causeway from Singapore. The Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link to Woodlands is a major draw for new launches around the city centre and Bukit Chagar.
intro.KL City Centre: KL City Centre is the city's financial and lifestyle core around the Petronas Twin Towers and KL City Centre Park, with Jalan Ampang, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Embassy Row and Kampung Baru on its edges. Most projects here are high-rise suites within walking distance of an LRT or MRT station.
intro.Kebun Teh: Kebun Teh is a residential area north of Johor Bahru city centre, close to the Johor Bahru Eastern Dispersal Link.
intro.Kelantan: Kota Bharu is the capital of Kelantan, with Kubang Kerian as its medical and university hub.
intro.Kota Kinabalu: Kota Kinabalu is Sabah's capital, with a city-centre waterfront, malls and the international airport close by.
intro.Kuala Lumpur: Kuala Lumpur is Malaysia's capital and its busiest new-launch market, from KL City Centre and TRX to Bukit Bintang, Bangsar, Bukit Jalil and Taman Desa, all linked by the MRT, LRT and Monorail network.
intro.Kuala Terengganu: Kuala Terengganu is the capital of Terengganu, with a waterfront city centre, Chinatown and boat links to the islands.
intro.Kubang Kerian: Kubang Kerian in Kota Bharu is home to Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia and its health campus.
intro.Kwasa Damansara: Kwasa Damansara is a planned transit-oriented city in Selangor with two MRT stations, Kwasa Damansara and Kwasa Sentral, next to Kota Damansara.
intro.Melaka: Melaka City is a UNESCO World Heritage city and one of Malaysia's leading domestic tourism destinations.
intro.Melaka City: Melaka City is a UNESCO World Heritage city and a leading tourism destination.
intro.Paya Terubong: Paya Terubong is a hillside residential area in central Penang island, near Farlim and Air Itam.
intro.Penang: Penang combines a UNESCO heritage city in George Town with an industrial and tech hub around Bayan Lepas and Batu Kawan, and new homes on both the island and the mainland.
intro.Petaling Jaya: Petaling Jaya is Selangor's established city next to Kuala Lumpur, with mature neighbourhoods, malls, LRT and MRT stations and many schools.
intro.Sabah: Kota Kinabalu is Sabah's capital and the gateway to East Malaysia, with a growing waterfront city centre.
intro.Selangor: Selangor surrounds Kuala Lumpur and offers more space for the money, with new townships such as Kwasa Damansara and established addresses in Petaling Jaya, Damansara and Subang Jaya.
intro.Subang Jaya: Subang Jaya is a mature Selangor city with Sunway, SS15 and USJ, served by the LRT and the BRT Sunway line.
intro.TRX: Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) is Kuala Lumpur's new international financial district, built around the Exchange 106 tower, The Exchange TRX mall and a large MRT interchange.
intro.Taman Desa: Taman Desa is a mature neighbourhood off Jalan Klang Lama, close to Mid Valley and Bangsar, with easy access to several highways.
intro.Tanjung Bungah: Tanjung Bungah is a coastal suburb on Penang island's north coast, between Gurney and Batu Ferringhi.
intro.Terengganu: Kuala Terengganu is the capital of Terengganu on the east coast, known for its waterfront, Chinatown and islands.
